en: Itivuttaka 18:
Ekakanipāta,
Second Chapter (Dutiyavagga)
The Discourse on Schism in the Sangha.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:

"Bhikkhus, one thing, when it arises in the world, arises for the harm of many people, for the unhappiness of many people, for the ruin, harm, and suffering of many people, including gods and humans."
What is that one thing?
It is schism in the Saṅgha.
When the Saṅgha is split, monks, there arise mutual quarrels, mutual insults, mutual censures, and mutual exclusions.
"In that regard, those who have no faith do not become faithful, and some of those who are already faithful undergo a change of heart.
The Blessed One said this.
Concerning this, it is said:
“Subject to states of deprivation, destined for hell,
remaining there for an eon is the schism-maker of the Saṅgha;
delighting in factions, established in what is not Dhamma.”
Falls away from security from bondage;
having split a harmonious Saṅgha,
one will boil in hell for an eon.”
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The eighth.
